transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-08
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Meridian CISO), Ben Torres (Procurement), Ravi Patel (Cloud Architect)

Summary:
Redwood AE/SE walked Meridian Bank through the SIG/CAIQ questionnaire, discussed what evidence Meridian typically requires, clarified SOC 2 / ISO attestation availability, SSO/RBAC patterns, audit logging, encryption/KMS options, and private deployment concerns. Action items include uploading completed SIG, sharing SOC2/ISO docs, exchanging SSO metadata, and scheduling a technical deep dive.

Topics covered (rough): SOC 2 attestation; ISO 27001; RBAC and SAML details; audit log formats and retention; KMS/HSM integration and key custody; data residency and private/VPC options; timing for evidence delivery.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 55 minutes slotted. Quick intros?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Hi this is Aisha, CISO at Meridian. Thanks for doing this, we've got the vendor risk team and procurement on the call.
[00:14] Ben Torres: Ben from procurement, hi.
[00:16] Dev Patel: Dev, SE from Redwood, hey everyone.
[00:19] Ravi Patel: Ravi, cloud architect, thanks.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: Great. So the goal for today is to walk through the SIG/CAIQ, call out where we can point to evidence, and surface any gaps for Meridian's vendor risk team. We'll also chat about SOC 2, ISO, encryption, and SSO.
[00:36] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. We flagged a few high-priority items: encryption at rest keys, KMS/HSM, audit log retention and format, and whether Redwood's hosted offering keeps data in US-only regions or if we can ensure EU residency. Also SSO and RBAC for administrative users.
[00:51] Dev Patel: Understood. I'll jump in on the technical pieces. Quick note, some of the product names on the questionnaire map to our internal names, sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'Redwood runtime' in the doc, but it's Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Runtime.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: Yes we saw 'redwood runtime' which was ambiguous, thanks for clarifying. For KMS, we need to know if keys are customer-managed or service-managed and if there's HSM-backed key storage.
[01:16] Dev Patel: Right, good question. For the hosted API we offer integration with customer-managed KMS for enterprise plans - we can integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP KMS. Keys are customer-provided and we support envelope encryption patterns. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can bring-your-own-HSM; for hosted we also offer a managed KMS but for regulated customers we recommend CMKs in their account.
[01:40] Aisha Khan: So for evidence, can you provide an architecture diagram showing where keys live, and a statement about HSM usage?
[01:47] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we can add an architecture doc and a redacted HSM attestation note. We'll include what we typically provide: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert copy, and a KMS integration doc.
[01:58] Ben Torres: On audit logs: the questionnaire asks for examples of audit logs and retention periods, we need to show log formats (JSON) and where logs are stored and who can access them.
[02:08] Dev Patel: We can provide sanitized sample audit logs in JSON. Logs include request metadata, model variant, timestamp, routing decision, and low-level error codes. For PII-sensitive content we redact the request bodies in shared samples. Retention: hosted offering retains detailed request logs for 30 days by default, with configurable retention for enterprise customers and options to stream logs to customer S3/GCS for long-term retention. For Dedicated/Private you control retention fully.
[02:35] Ravi Patel: Can you stream logs into our AWS account or do you keep a copy?
[02:39] Dev Patel: We support log forwarding to customer-managed buckets or SIEMs via secure connectors and can set up cross-account replication so you own the primary copy. For compliance, audit logs are also replicated in our control plane for three months for troubleshooting, but can be restricted subject to contract.
[02:56] Aisha Khan: What about RBAC and admin access - we need separation of duties and proof of role-based controls. Is there SSO and SAML?
[03:04] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we support SSO with SAML2.0 and OIDC. On enterprise plans we enable SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC with predefined roles and custom roles for admin/read-only/audit. We also have org-level and project-level controls.
[03:18] Dev Patel: To add, actions by admins are logged and we have admin activity audit logs separate from API request logs. Those logs show who changed rollouts, who created keys, et cetera.
[03:29] Ben Torres: Do you have attestations for access reviews and provisioning processes?
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: Our SOC 2 cover access controls and provisioning processes; we can point to control mappings in the SIG. We'll include the SOC 2 section that maps to 'user provisioning' and 'access reviews'.
[03:45] Ravi Patel: Data residency - we need to lock production data in EU datacenters. Does Redwood support region pinning for hosted?
[03:52] Dev Patel: Yes, we support region pinning for enterprise customers on hosted with EU-only regions. For stronger guarantees we recommend Redwood Dedicated in a customer-specific VPC or the private deployment option where the control plane is customer-managed.
[04:07] Aisha Khan: For private deployment, the questionnaire asks about network isolation and patching responsibilities. How do you handle patching for on-prem or private?
[04:15] Dev Patel: For private on-prem we offer two modes: customer-managed where you run the runtime and we provide images and patch notes, or a managed private mode where Redwood operates the runtime inside your network under an SLA. We provide a patch schedule and can do emergency patches via a process defined in the contract. We'll provide the standard runbook and maintenance windows.
[04:35] Ben Torres: Regarding penetration testing and vulnerability scans, do you provide recent pen test reports or do you permit customer-conducted tests?
[04:42] Lena Ortiz: We can share redacted external pen test summaries. For customer-initiated assessments, we have a process in the vendor security form; usually we do a questionnaire to scope the test, and for Dedicated/Private we allow customer testing with approved windows and guardrails.
[04:56] Aisha Khan: On the SIG: there are several control IDs where Meridian needs evidence links. Can you call out which fields you'll populate vs which require us to supply more context?
[05:04] Lena Ortiz: Sure. We typically populate the operational controls around availability, incident response, encryption and key management, and supply links to SOC 2/ISO documents. Items that require customer input are things like their legal residency preferences, their specific contractual retention terms, and whether they need logs forwarded to their SIEM. We'll mark those as 'customer action'.
[05:22] Dev Patel: I'll go row-by-row live: For the encryption at rest control, we'll add a link to our KMS integration doc and upload a redacted architecture diagram. For network isolation, we'll attach our VPC design for Dedicated and the private deployment network diagram. For key custody we indicate support for customer-managed CMKs and BYO-HSM for Private.
[05:41] Ravi Patel: Good. For the 'key rotation' control, what's the default rotation policy?
[05:45] Dev Patel: By default our managed keys rotate every 90 days; if you BYOK then rotation is on your side and we won’t rotate your master key, but we support rotating data keys via envelope encryption. We'll document that in the SIG row.
[05:58] Ben Torres: The procurement team will need a copy of the SOC 2 Type II report - can you provide a redacted PDF via secure link?
[06:04] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we'll provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate via a secure share (DocuShare link). We'll add that link to the SIG evidence column.
[06:13] Aisha Khan: On SSO metadata exchange, our IdP requires a SAML metadata file and SP endpoints. Is that something Redwood can provide now to test?
[06:21] Dev Patel: Yes, we can provide SAML SP metadata and a test IdP configuration. We'll exchange metadata after the call. One note: provisioning with SCIM may require a separate enablement ticket.
[06:32] Ravi Patel: For logging formats, can we get a sample of the 'routing decision' field you mentioned? We want to see how you record model variant and fallback events.
[06:39] Dev Patel: Absolutely. The sample will show fields: request_id, timestamp, user_id_hash, model_variant, routing_policy, fallback_trigger, latency_ms, node_id. We'll sanitize IDs.
[06:50] Ben Torres: For data deletion and retention requests from regulators, what's the process and SLA?
[06:55] Lena Ortiz: For standard hosted customers we have a 30 day deletion window for request processing; for enterprise we offer expedited deletion and can add contract language for regulators. For Dedicated/Private, deletion is customer-controlled. We'll capture this in the SIG and include the data-deletion runbook.
[07:10] Aisha Khan: One more: who has access to raw request payloads in your operations team? We need to know the blurb for least privilege.
[07:18] Dev Patel: Access is strictly on a least-privilege basis, via role-based access and time-limited jumpboxes. Only designated SREs with approval can access raw payloads and those accesses are logged and require approval. We'll include an access control matrix snippet.
[07:32] Lena Ortiz: Ok we're about 45 minutes in, starting to wrap. I'll summarize next steps and we can capture action items.
[07:38] Lena Ortiz: Action items: Redwood uploads SIG/CAIQ filled spreadsheet with evidence links, uploads SOC2/ISO docs, Dev to prepare sample logs, and schedule a technical deep dive for private deployment if Meridian wants it.
[07:50] Ravi Patel: Sounds good, can we request the tech deep dive focus on patching and network isolation?
[07:55] Dev Patel: Yes we can do a 60-90 minute SE-led deep dive to go over the runtime, patching cadence, and network topology.
[08:02] Ben Torres: Procurement will follow up once evidence is posted and then route the questionnaire for internal review.
[08:08] Aisha Khan: Thanks all. One clarification: please mark the SOC2 report as 'redacted' and indicate the control mapping in the SIG rows so our risk folks can correlate quickly.
[08:18] Lena Ortiz: Will do. I'll add notes in the SIG and include a control map.
[08:22] Lena Ortiz: Any final questions?
[08:24] Ravi Patel: Not from me.
[08:26] Ben Torres: Nope.
[08:27] Aisha Khan: That's it. Thank you.
[08:29] Lena Ortiz: Great, we'll send the links and schedule the deep dive, thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
